description: oauth.WithStateSigningKey is opt-in, so by default the OAuth state cookie (oauth/state.go packState/unpackState, wired by oauth/handlers.go setStateCookie) is an unauthenticated 5-field value: state, PKCE verifier, OIDC nonce, provider, tenant. Without a key, unpackState accepts any well-formed self-minted value, so anyone with a cookie-write primitive (subdomain sharing a parent Domain via WithCookieDomain, or plaintext HTTP when WithInsecureCookies is set) can forge the state/provider/tenant binding the callback trusts (stateMatches + provider/tenant equality checks). The default cookie name 'oauth_state' is not __Host- prefixed, which widens the cookie-tossing precondition when a parent Domain is configured. PoC (worktree, httptest only): a self-minted cookie 'attacker-state...<b64 test>.<b64 empty>' paired with ?state=attacker-state&code=... reaches the token exchange and drives issuance (204 + auth cookies) without a signing key, while the identical forgery with WithStateSigningKey configured is rejected 403 invalid_state.
remediation: Fail closed or warn loudly when no state signing key is configured: require WithStateSigningKey (or derive it from the tenant keystore) for production use, emit a startup/misuse event when unsigned, and consider a __Host- prefixed default state-cookie name so shared-Domain deployments stay host-locked. At minimum, document that WithCookieDomain + unsigned state cookies re-opens login-CSRF/provider-confusion via subdomain cookie-tossing.
title: OAuth state cookie unsigned by default: forged provider/tenant binding accepted

description: When neither oauth.WithRedirectURL nor oauth.WithAllowedHosts is set, handlerConfig.resolveRedirectURL (oauth/handlers.go) builds redirect_uri as requestScheme(r)+'://'+r.Host+r.URL.Path, where requestScheme trusts the spoofable X-Forwarded-Proto header and r.Host is the raw Host header (isValidHost only checks syntax). The resulting attacker-influenced redirect_uri is sent to the provider in AuthCodeURL and reused in the code exchange. Exploitation additionally requires the provider to honor an unregistered redirect_uri (most strict providers reject it, which bounds severity to Low), plus a Host-poisoning primitive (misbehaving proxy) or a victim clicking a link whose Host the attacker controls at the network edge. PoC (worktree, httptest only): BeginHandler with no redirect/allowlist options and Host 'evil.example' + X-Forwarded-Proto 'https' emits a 302 whose redirect_uri starts with 'https://evil.example/'; the same request with WithAllowedHosts('app.example.com') is rejected 400.
remediation: Require an explicit redirect_uri (WithRedirectURL) or allowlist (WithAllowedHosts) in production: log/emit a misuse event when falling back to Host-derived redirect_uri, never trust X-Forwarded-Proto unless the deployment declares a trusted proxy, and document that the Host-derived fallback is dev-only. Consider rejecting the fallback outright when the request is not loopback/TLS.
